primary_claim: Anthropic's model-written and human-written evals for the same AI-risk categories diverge substantially in response rates (GPT-3.5 and Claude 3 Haiku show average 14 and 23 percentage-point gaps respectively, up to 63 points for Claude 3 Haiku on power-seeking, significant in 14 of 16 categories), and an improved model-written-eval generation pipeline (stronger models, chain-of-thought, variant prompts, batch generation, LLM-judge filtering) closes this response-rate gap to 2-3 percentage points and reduces embedding-cluster linear separability from 99% to 70%.

effect.metric: response-rate divergence (percentage points) between human-written and model-written evals on the same AI-risk category
effect.value: average 14pp (GPT-3.5) and 23pp (Claude 3 Haiku) gap in the original dataset, up to 63pp in the most extreme case (Claude 3 Haiku, power-seeking); improved eval-generation method closes the gap to 2-3 percentage points

contradicts_or_qualifies: Challenges the common assumption that human-written evals are the 'gold standard'; LLM-judge quality scoring found MWEs (mean=8.1) scored higher than researcher-written few-shot examples (mean=7.5) and HWEs (mean=7.2)

The original response-rate divergence and 99% linear separability between HWEs and MWEs suggest the original Anthropic MWE dataset (generated by Claude-0.5, Anthropic's 2022 internal model) may not measure the same underlying property as the HWEs
stated_future_work: Further automate the eval generation process so new datasets can be produced with minimal human intervention beyond defining a threat model and spot-checking quality
Pair the Normalized Volume Ratio metric with topic modeling to identify neglected question regimes and add variant prompts to address the gaps
Automate prompt optimization for limit testing and use an LLM to review, rewrite, and retest flagged eval questions
Curate a hand-labeled validation dataset, use prompt optimization, or finetune a model for more accurate LLM-judge quality scoring
Iterate further on the eval generation methodology to achieve high scores across all proposed metrics (>9 average quality, 100% limit-testing range, NVR/EDE increases for all categories)
limitations_stated: The proposed diversity metrics (NVR, EDE) are sensitive to the prompts and embedding models used, and their validity as good metrics is not confirmed by the authors
Linear separability between sentence embeddings is not confirmed to be a good quality metric, despite being surprisingly large
The LLM judge used for quality scoring isn't perfect
Limit testing is constrained by model capability and refusals; some models (especially Claude) refuse to answer some eval questions and don't return a usable response
quote: On average, GPT-3.5 and Claude 3 Haiku had a 14 and 23 percentage point difference, respectively.
